rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so this round shifts weight toward stronger obfuscation while respecting the program's constraints: allroots is a tiny (205-line, 7-function, ~2.4 KB text) numeric kernel with hot iteration loops (allroots/newton/HORNERS), so cheap, loop-safe transforms are favored. SUB gets the highest security/diversity weights because arithmetic obfuscation composes well with the integer-heavy dispatch and index math here at near-zero cost, and its low cost weights let it apply broadly. FLA and BCF are weighted strongly to target the largest functions (deflat, main, allroots), where control-flow flattening and bogus branches yield the most analyst confusion, with moderate cost weights to avoid bloating the tiny binary or slowing the inner numeric loops. SPLIT stays enabled as a low-risk size multiplier that helps FLA distribute blocks. IBR is kept moderately weighted to break static CFG recovery, but its cost weights temper application inside hot loops. ICALL and IGV carry the highest correctness-risk weight (indirect-call lowering and global-variable encoding interact badly with the floating-point-heavy, pointer-sensitive code and add per-call indirection), so they are permitted only where features strongly favor them rather than applied broadly. Overall the table trades a modest runtime/size budget for substantially higher security and diversity than round 0, relying on the measured correctness success to justify the push.
